content: 1. Correa GC et al. (2007) conducted a study on the use of buprenorphine-naloxone treatment for opioid-dependent inmates in Puerto Rico prior to their release. The findings were published in the Journal of Addiction Medicine. 2. Hedrich D, Alves P, et al. (2012) systematically reviewed the effectiveness of opioid maintenance treatment in prison settings. Their research, published in Addiction, highlights the potential benefits of such interventions in reducing opioid dependency among incarcerated populations. 3. Sacks JY, McKendrick K, et al. (2012) performed a randomized clinical trial to evaluate therapeutic community treatment for female inmates. The study assessed outcomes at six and twelve months post-release and was published in the Journal of Addictive Diseases. 4. Springer SA, Chen S, et al. (2010) demonstrated improved outcomes in HIV and substance abuse treatment for HIV-infected prisoners released from incarceration when buprenorphine treatment was utilized. This study appeared in the Journal of Urban Health. 5. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) (2013) reported on the implementation of opioid substitution therapy (OST) in Tihar prisons, India. This scientific report was published by UNODC in Vienna. 6. Freudenberg N, Ramaswamy M, et al. (2010) evaluated the REAL MEN re-entry program, which aimed to reduce drug use, HIV risk, and recidivism among young men leaving jail. The findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health. 7. De la Fuente L, Bravo MJ, et al. (2012) analyzed the evolution of opioid substitution treatment and needle exchange programs in Spanish prisons from 1992 to 2009. Their findings were published in the Spanish Journal of Penitentiary Health. 8. Bachireddy C, Bazazi AR, et al. (2011) explored attitudes toward opioid substitution therapy and pre-incarceration HIV transmission behaviors among HIV-infected prisoners in Malaysia. The study, published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence, discusses implications for secondary prevention. 9. Favrod-Coune T, Baroundi M, et al. (2013) presented a case study on opioid substitution treatment in pretrial prison detention in Geneva, Switzerland. The findings were published in the Swiss Medical Weekly. 10. Eshrati B, Asl RT, et al. (2008) provided initial evidence supporting harm reduction education to prevent HIV transmission among Iranian prisoners. The study was published in the Harm Reduction Journal. 11. Derlega VJ, Winstead BA, et al. (2008) examined the stigma associated with AIDS among inmates and staff in a U.S. state prison. The findings were published in the Journal of STD and AIDS. 12. Fields J, Gonzalez I, et al. (2008) discussed the importance of learning from and engaging with incarcerated women to address their unique health needs. 13. Sifunda S, Reddy PS, et al. (2008) evaluated the effectiveness of a peer-led HIV/AIDS and STI health education intervention for prison inmates. The study was published in Health Education and Behavior. 14. Ko NY, Hsu ST, et al. (2009) conducted a pilot study on the impact of HIV education on substance use readiness, AIDS knowledge, and self-efficacy for risk reduction among male drug-dependent inmates. The findings were published in Substance Use and Misuse. 15. Grinstead O, Eldridge G, et al. (2008) developed and evaluated Project START, an HIV, STD, and hepatitis prevention program for young men leaving prison. The study was published in the Journal of Correctional Health Care. 16. Fluhmann P, Wassmer M, et al. (2012) emphasized the importance of structured information exchange on infectious diseases for prisoners. Their findings were published in the Journal of Correctional Health Care. 17. Goldberg E, Millson P, et al. (2009) conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess an HIV risk reduction intervention for incarcerated youth. The study was published in the Journal of Adolescent Health. 18. Gurdin J, Niego S, et al. (2008) described the Rikers Health Advocacy Program (RHAP), an STI/HIV/AIDS prevention program for young men, as part of evidence-based interventions for adolescent sexual health. 19. Hurd NM, Valerio MN, et al. (2010) adapted an HIV prevention intervention for high-risk, incarcerated adolescents. The findings were published in Health Education and Behavior. 20. Martin S, O’Connell D, et al. (2008) integrated an HIV/HCV brief intervention into prisoner re-entry programs. The results of this multisite prospective study were published in the Journal of Psychoactive Drugs. 21. La Vigne NG, Debus-Sherrill S, et al. (2011) proposed a situational crime prevention approach to reduce violence and sexual assault in jails. 22. Yap L, Richters J, et al. (2011) documented a decline in sexual assaults in men’s prisons in New South Wales, attributing the success to a systems approach. The study was published in the Journal of Interpersonal Violence. 23. Ravi A, Blankenship KM, et al. (2007) explored health issues specific to incarcerated women, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. 24. Kerbs JJ, Jolley JM (2007) investigated inmate-on-inmate victimization among older male prisoners. The findings were published in Crime and Delinquency. 25. Kavasery R, Maru DS, et al. (2009) conducted a prospective controlled trial of routine opt-out HIV testing in a female jail setting. The study was published in PLoS One. 26. Duffus WA, Youmans E (2009) highlighted missed opportunities for early HIV diagnosis in correctional facilities. The findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs. 27. Jafa K, McElroy P, et al. (2009) emphasized the importance of early identification of HIV through jail-based testing. The study was published in PLoS One. 28. Motshabi LC, Pengpid S, et al. (2011) examined the utilization and attitudes toward HIV counseling and testing among male inmates in a South African prison. The findings were published in the Journal of Social Aspects of HIV/AIDS. 29. De Voux A, Spaulding AC, et al. (2012) provided empirical support for jail-based HIV testing as a means of early identification. The study was published in PLoS One. 30. UNODC, UNAIDS, WHO (2009) released a technical paper on HIV testing and counseling in prisons and closed settings. 31. Beckwith CG, Liu T, et al. (2010) analyzed changes in HIV risk behavior before and after counseling and testing in jail. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 32. MacGowan R, Margolis A, et al. (2009) evaluated voluntary rapid HIV testing in jails. The findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 33. Beckwith CG, Bazerman L, et al. (2011) assessed a routine opt-out rapid HIV testing program in Rhode Island. The study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention. 34. Tartaro C, Levy MP (2012) evaluated an HIV testing program in a jail setting, providing results and recommendations. The findings were published in The Prison Journal. 35. Andrinopoulos K, Kerrigan D, et al. (2010) established an HIV/STD program and assessed infection prevalence among incarcerated men in Jamaica. The study was published in the International Journal of STD and AIDS. 36. Arp W (2009) discussed the intersection of race, incarceration, and HIV/AIDS in Louisiana, advocating for mandatory testing due to risky sexual behavior. The findings were published in Race, Class, and Gender. 37. Kavasery R, Maru DS, et al. (2009) conducted a prospective controlled trial of routine opt-out HIV testing in a men’s jail. The study was published in PLoS One. 38. Strick LB, MacGowan J, et al. (2011) reported on HIV screening of male inmates during prison intake medical evaluations in Washington from 2006 to 2010. The findings were published in the MMWR. 39. Javanbakht M, Murphy R, et al. (2007) examined the prevalence of sexually transmitted infections and HIV among incarcerated men who have sex with men from 2000 to 2005. The study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 40. Tuli K, Kerndt PR (2009) conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of preventing sexually transmitted infections among incarcerated men who have sex with men. The findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 41. Roberson DW, White BL (2009) identified factors influencing adherence to antiretroviral therapy among HIV-infected female inmates. The study was published in the Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care. 42. Small W, Wood E, et al. (2009) explored the impact of incarceration on adherence to HIV treatment among HIV-positive injection drug users. The findings were published in AIDS Care. 43. Shalihu N, Pretorius L, et al. (2014) described barriers to antiretroviral therapy adherence among Namibian prisoners. The study was published in AIDS Care. 44. Catz SL, Thibodeau L, et al. (2011) identified the prevention needs of HIV-positive men and women awaiting release from prison. The findings were published in AIDS Behavior. 45. Fontana L, Beckerman A (2007) highlighted the primary care treatment needs and experiences of recently released individuals with HIV/AIDS. The study was published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved. 46. Wohl DA, Scheyett A, et al. (2011) compared intensive case management with comprehensive pre-release discharge planning for linking HIV-infected prisoners to care. The study was published in AIDS Behavior. 47. Nunn A, Cornwall A, et al. (2010) assessed the COMPASS program, which links HIV-positive jail inmates to treatment, care, and social services post-release. The findings were published in the Journal of Urban Health. 48. Zaller ND, Holmes L, et al. (2008) evaluated Project Bridge, which provides linkage to treatment and supportive services for HIV-positive ex-offenders. The study was published in the Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved. 49. Seal DW, Margolis AD, et al. (2008) examined substance use and sexual behavior during incarceration among young men aged 18 to 29. The findings were published in AIDS Behavior. 50. Milloy MJ, Kerr T, et al. (2013) found that incarceration is associated with syringe lending among active injection drug users with detectable plasma HIV-1 RNA. The study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases. 51. Moller LF, Van Den Bergh BJ, et al. (2008) studied the effects of health promotion on drug use in Kyrgyzstan prisons. The findings were published in the International Journal of Prisoner Health. 52. Roshanfekr P, Farnia M, et al. (2013) evaluated the effectiveness of harm reduction programs in seven Iranian prisons. The study was published in the Iranian Journal of Public Health. 53. Ferrer-Castro V, Crespo-Leiro MR, et al. (2012) reviewed a ten-year needle exchange program at Pereiro de Aguiar prison in Spain. The findings were published in the Spanish Journal of Penitentiary Health.
